subject: Governmental Transparency and Budgetary Oversight Reforms
overview: The Council debated a major resolution regarding structural government reforms and the balance of power between the legislative and executive branches. Members also processed several significant financial appropriations following the certification of $25 million in free cash, including funding for fire trucks and infrastructure equipment.

items.title: Tributes and Commendations
items.summary: The Council offered condolences to the family of Vincent DiClemente and congratulated Joan Gatto on being named Citizen of the Year.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Records of the February 28, 2023, meeting were approved.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council accepted reports from the Committee of the Whole and subcommittees regarding food trucks, waste hauler ordinances, tree ordinances, and outdoor dining.

items.title: ARPA Expenditure Breakdown
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a dollar-for-dollar breakdown and audit of all ARPA funds spent by the administration to date.

items.title: Local Maintenance and Illegal Dumping
items.summary: The Council passed resolutions calling for pothole repairs on Lawrence Road and the removal of illegally dumped items on Doonan Street.

items.title: Agenda and Meeting Management Software
items.summary: Approved the implementation of Civic Clerk software to streamline council agendas, public document access, and meeting transparency.

items.title: Resolution on Pesticides and Rodenticides
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state bills HD 577 and SD 1144 to restrict certain pesticides following the recent poisoning of a local bald eagle.

items.title: Zoning Process and Legal Counsel
items.summary: Requested funding for specialized legal and planning counsel to complete the city's zoning recodification process.

items.title: Capital Improvement Plan Update
items.summary: Requested an updated presentation from the administration on the city's long-term Capital Improvement Plan.

items.title: Governmental Structural Reforms
items.summary: Referred to the Committee of the Whole a resolution to discuss increasing Council authority over the budget, hiring independent Council staff, and requiring confirmation for board appointees. Councilors and the Chief of Staff debated the current balance of power and lack of collaboration between the executive and legislative branches.

items.title: Sidewalk Construction and Equipment Loan Order
items.summary: Approved for first reading a $1.5 million loan order for sidewalk repairs and specialized DPW equipment.

items.title: Fire Department Pumper Trucks
items.summary: Approved the appropriation of $2 million from free cash to purchase two pumper trucks for the fire department to avoid further manufacturing delays.

items.title: Non-Union Personnel Wage Adjustment
items.summary: Approved for first reading a series of 2% cost-of-living adjustments for non-union personnel backdated to 2021. The motion was amended to exclude the Mayor and City Council from the increases.

items.title: DPW and Fire Vehicle Appropriations
items.summary: Approved free cash expenditures for an electric street sweeper and several utility trucks for the DPW and Fire departments. The Council tabled the portion of the request related to non-union wage funding until updated figures are provided by the administration.

items.title: General Stabilization Fund
items.summary: Referred to the Committee of the Whole a proposal to establish a General Stabilization Fund with an initial $5 million appropriation from free cash.

items.title: 10-Year Waste Collection Agreement
items.summary: Tabled a request to authorize a 10-year solid waste collection contract pending a legal opinion on Council oversight and the necessity of a new vote.

items.title: Records Disposal
items.summary: Several outdated items from 2021 and 2022 were received and placed on file.
